rule: A charity receiving most or all income from the state is not automatically reclassified by SIDONIE; legal charity status and financial dependence are separate fields.
Public-income dependence is measured from reconciled accounts, not inferred from institutional type.
National Lottery proceeds remain distinguishable from taxpayer money even when a combined public-income metric is also useful.
Contracts for services and grants are separate where accounts disclose them.
An exempt charity's principal regulator is recorded; absence from the ordinary charity register is not treated as non-charitable status.
Central-government grant, locally raised council tax/business rates and retained income remain distinguishable where source data permit.
Council cultural expenditure is recorded by service line and year; a single 'culture spend' total is derived, never manually entered as the only fact.
Gross expenditure, net expenditure, income and capital are not mixed.
Changes in accounting/service definitions create a comparability flag rather than a false time series.
